searchText: I did some benchmarks for bls ecmul in gnark for glv, double-and-add and subgroup checks. ``` BenchmarkG1JacScalarMultiplication/double_and_add_(2_bit_window)-12 9188 124130 ns/op BenchmarkG1JacScalarMultiplication/GLV-12 15762 75613 ns/op BenchmarkG1JacScalarMultiplication/subgroup_check-12 21189 56661 ns/op ... BenchmarkG2JacScalarMultiplication/double_and_add_(2_bit_windowed)-12 3000 403193 ns/op BenchmarkG2JacScalarMultiplication/GLV-12 5066 236869 ns/op BenchmarkG2JacScalarMultiplication/subgroup_check-12 14960 82193 ns/op ``` so keeping subgroup checks for mul makes sense with gnark i think it was for MSM. The gas formula is sublinear (and too steep) but on their benchmark, MSM + N subgroup checks have a linear cost. can you show the code used for double_and_add_2_bit_window? Is it using wNAF? no NAF: https://github.com/Consensys/gnark-crypto/blob/master/ecc/bls12-381/g1.go#L505-L537 BenchmarkG1JacScalarMultiplication/GLV <- This is without subgroup checks? and BenchmarkG1JacScalarMultiplication/subgroup_check <- This is GLV with subgroup checks? ah... sorry, it's confusing: `*subgroup_check` is only the subgroup check. `GLV`/`double_and_add...` are multiplication without subgroup check. https://github.com/jwasinger/gnark-crypto/tree/subgroup-check-bench So without subgroup check, a regular scalar multiplication without the glv optimization is `124,130 ns/op` The subgroup check costs `56661 ns/op` and the glv version of scalar multiplication costs `75613 ns/op` so altogether the cost would be `132,274 ns/op` Does that sound correct? Thanks for the link -- so I would draw the opposite conclusion from those benchmarks then; if the subgroup check is needed with glv, then its not better than having no subgroup check without glv optimization > keeping subgroup checks for mul makes sense with gnark That was the same opinion I was trying to express "from geth pov: keeping subgroup checks for the mul precompile makes sense if we use gnark/GLV" - is what I meant to convey Those are my bench in cosntantine. subgroup check + GLV + wNAF is faster than a naive double-and-add but slower that plain wNAF.

excerpts.author: jwasinger
excerpts.content:
I did some benchmarks for bls ecmul in gnark for glv, double-and-add and subgroup checks.
```
BenchmarkG1JacScalarMultiplication/double_and_add_(2_bit_window)-12                 9188        124130 ns/op
BenchmarkG1JacScalarMultiplication/GLV-12                                          15762         75613 ns/op
BenchmarkG1JacScalarMultiplication/subgroup_check-12                               21189         56661 ns/op
...
BenchmarkG2JacScalarMultiplication/double_and_add_(2_bit_windowed)-12                 3000        403193 ns/op
BenchmarkG2JacScalarMultiplication/GLV-12                                             5066        236869 ns/op
BenchmarkG2JacScalarMultiplication/subgroup_check-12                                 14960         82193 ns/op
```

excerpts.author: jwasinger
excerpts.content: so keeping subgroup checks for mul makes sense with gnark

excerpts.author: mratsim
excerpts.content:
i think it was for MSM.

The gas formula is sublinear (and too steep) but on their benchmark, MSM + N subgroup checks have a linear cost.

excerpts.author: jwasinger
excerpts.content: ah... sorry, it's confusing:  `*subgroup_check` is only the subgroup check.  `GLV`/`double_and_add...` are multiplication without subgroup check.

excerpts.author: kevaundray
excerpts.content:
So without subgroup check, a regular scalar multiplication without the glv optimization is `124,130 ns/op`

The subgroup check costs `56661 ns/op` and the glv version of scalar multiplication costs `75613 ns/op` so altogether the cost would be `132,274 ns/op`

Does that sound correct?

excerpts.author: kevaundray
excerpts.content: Thanks for the link -- so I would draw the opposite conclusion from those benchmarks then; if the subgroup check is needed with glv, then its not better than having no subgroup check without glv optimization
